articles.title: Coronal Plane Alignment of the Knee (CPAK) in children and adolescents : an analysis of 655 knees according to the CPAK classification.
articles.authors: Pott H, Savov P, Stauss R, Chen DB, MacDessi SJ, Ettinger M
articles.population: Children and adolescents aged 4 to 18 years
articles.outcomes: Coronal plane alignment measurements using CPAK classification, hip-knee-ankle angle, and joint line obliquity
articles.take_home: As children grow, their knee alignment stays relatively stable overall, but the angle of the joint line changes significantly towards a different shape. The most common knee alignment type in children and adolescents was CPAK III, accounting for just over half of all knees studied.

articles.title: The Effect of Flexible Suture Button Fixation on the Reduction of the Syndesmosis: A Cadaver Study.
articles.authors: Roward L, Reynolds Z, Harris J, Jeray K, Jd Adams JD Jr
articles.outcomes: Syndesmotic reduction measured by translation (mm) and rotation (degrees) on CT imaging; comparison of quadricortical versus tricortical suture button placement
articles.take_home: A flexible suture button device improved poorly positioned ankle syndesmosis by about 3 mm and 10 degrees of rotation during surgery. Whether the button was placed through four or three layers of bone did not make a meaningful difference to how much improvement was achieved.

articles.title: Age-related differences in radiologic and clinical presentation of Charcot-Marie-Tooth foot deformity: Insights from WBCT and PROMIS analysis.
articles.authors: Song JH, Michalski MP, Porter GM, Tong A, Pfeffer GB
articles.outcomes: 3D foot structure measurements from weightbearing CT scans and PROMIS pain interference scores
articles.take_home: Adults with CMT had flatter foot arches and more pain than children, whilst children had more twisted midfoot and heel deformities. The study shows that CMT foot problems change and typically worsen as patients get older.

articles.title: Posterior and anterior malleolus fixation is associated with lower syndesmosis malreduction rates.
articles.outcomes: Syndesmotic reduction accuracy assessed by CT imaging; rates of syndesmotic malreduction
articles.take_home: Fixing both the posterior and anterior ankle bones together gave the best results, with no cases of poor alignment, compared to 29% of patients who had neither fixed. Fixing just the posterior bone was also helpful, reducing poor alignment to 10%.

articles.title: Comparative performance of large language models for foot and ankle clinical decision support: A multi-rater evaluation of seven models.
articles.authors: ParK KH, Shim DW, Lee JW, Kim HJ, Suh DH, Jeon Y, et al.
articles.population: Seven large language models tested on foot and ankle clinical questions
articles.sample_size: 20 multiple-choice questions and 20 open-ended clinical questions evaluated by three blinded foot and ankle surgeons
articles.outcomes: Multiple-choice question accuracy and open-ended response quality scores (range 3-21) for accuracy, completeness and clinical relevance
articles.take_home: Two AI models, GPT-5 Thinking and GPT-o3, performed best at answering foot and ankle clinical questions, achieving 95% accuracy on multiple-choice questions and the highest scores on complex clinical scenarios. However, the authors caution that AI models change rapidly, so these results should be seen as a snapshot of current performance rather than a permanent ranking.

articles.title: Effects of medializing calcaneal osteotomy and lateral column lengthening osteotomy variations on foot alignment: A three dimensional anatomical model study.
articles.authors: Davutluoglu E, Ozer M, Deniz Y, Aydin N, Aydingoz O, Ashkani-Esfahani S, et al.
articles.population: Patients with progressive collapsing foot deformity
articles.outcomes: Effects of medializing calcaneal osteotomy and lateral column lengthening osteotomy on foot alignment measurements including talus-first metatarsal angle, talonavicular coverage, hindfoot angle and talocalcaneal angle
articles.take_home: The study found that lateral column lengthening surgery corrects forefoot alignment whilst medializing calcaneal osteotomy corrects hindfoot alignment, with changes occurring in a predictable linear pattern depending on the size of the surgical correction. These findings may help surgeons plan foot surgery for rigid deformities but may not apply to flexible collapsed feet where soft tissue plays a larger role.
